title: One-Click Evernote Exit & Clean Markdown/Obsidian/Notion Migrator
oneLiner: Migrate 10+ years of Evernote notebooks, tags, and attachments into Notion, Obsidian, or Apple Notes cleanly—escaping $249/year renewals.
problemSummary: Long-time Evernote users are leaving in waves after subscription hikes jumped from $69–$130/yr toward $249.99/yr alongside intrusive upsell popups and editor scrolling glitches. Moving thousands of legacy ENEX notes without breaking attachments, creation dates, or nested tags remains painful.
targetAudience: Long-time Evernote subscribers (5–15 years of notes) switching to Obsidian, Notion, Craft, or Apple Notes

competitors.name: Evernote
competitors.weakness: Sharp annual price increases (up to $249.99/yr), aggressive paywall popups on note open, and typing/scrolling glitches.

mvpScope: Upload or drag-and-drop multiple .enex exports (local browser or desktop wrapper for privacy)
Preserve original created/updated timestamps, inline PDFs/images, checkboxes, and tag hierarchies
Export cleanly to Obsidian Markdown vault ZIP, Notion import bundle, or Apple Notes-ready HTML with a migration verification report
monetizationModel: Free up to 100 notes; $19–$29 one-time migration pass for unlimited notebooks

buildSpec.prd: Build a privacy-first Evernote (.enex) migration web app using Next.js + Web Workers (parsing XML in-browser so private notes never leave the user's machine). Show live stats of notes, attachments, broken links, and tags, then output a clean ZIP tailored for Obsidian, Notion, or Craft.
buildSpec.schema: tables: licenses (id, email, license_key, plan, purchased_at), migration_telemetry (id, target_app, note_count, attachment_count, duration_ms, created_at).
buildSpec.prompt: Build a Next.js + TypeScript client-side Evernote (.enex) converter. Parse ENEX XML inside a Web Worker using streaming XML parsing, convert ENML to clean Markdown with YAML frontmatter (title, created, updated, tags), extract base64 attachments into /attachments/ with clean filenames, and package a downloadable ZIP tailored for Obsidian or Notion.

evidence.quote: Been using Evernote for at least a decade. Bending Spoons made it better but they raised pricing from $69 to 129 a year, and now nearly doubling that to $249.99 a year!
evidence.author: ImranZ

evidence.quote: It used to be great, but now it’s really buggy, they jacked up the price, and I’m slowly transferring everything out of it. Great premise, destroyed!
evidence.author: Tiggermvs

evidence.quote: After two years of paying $130(!!!!!) a year which already seemed ridiculously high for a notes app, that particular 'plan' was eliminated and they automatically billed me at the new, more expensive plan which was NEARLY DOUBLE THE COST.
evidence.author: Britt Kaye

title: Cross-Agent Memory & Client Context Sync for Cursor, Claude Code & Codex
oneLiner: Maintain one shared source of truth for client rules, architectural decisions, and reusable skills across every AI coding tool.
problemSummary: Consultants and developers using multiple AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Claude Desktop) waste hours re-explaining client rules, past decisions, and custom skills every time they switch tools or hit rate limits.
targetAudience: AI-assisted freelance developers, dev agencies, and engineers switching between Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex

competitors.name: Claude Code
competitors.weakness: Skills and local context files do not automatically sync between Claude Desktop, Claude Code CLI, and other IDEs.

mvpScope: Web dashboard + lightweight CLI that stores per-client rules, architecture decisions, and reusable skills in Git-backed Markdown
One-command sync (`ctx sync`) that compiles rules into `.cursorrules`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and skill folders automatically
Encrypted team/client profiles so freelancers switch client contexts in one command without leaking rules across projects
monetizationModel: Free for 1 project; $12/mo solo pro or $39 one-time CLI + sync license

buildSpec.prd: Build a Next.js + Supabase dashboard paired with a Node.js CLI. Users define client workspaces containing architecture decisions, coding standards, and reusable skills. Running `ctx pull <client>` writes native config files for Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex while keeping changes versioned.
buildSpec.schema: tables: workspaces (id, owner_id, slug, name), context_blocks (id, workspace_id, category, title, content_md, updated_at), skills (id, workspace_id, name, content_md), sync_tokens (id, user_id, token_hash, last_used_at).
buildSpec.prompt: Build a Next.js + TypeScript + Supabase app and companion Node CLI that syncs AI coding context across Cursor (.cursor/rules), Claude Code (CLAUDE.md & skills), and Codex (AGENTS.md). Include client workspace isolation, version diffing, and one-command CLI pull/push.

evidence.quote: Like many of you I work with AI agents every day and across several clients. The major time cost for me is re-explaining context and past decisions, client rules, that we already do. Every tool has its own memory.
evidence.author: Michel_Aventin

evidence.quote: [FEATURE] Sync Skills between Claude Desktop and Claude Code CLI (173+ community upvotes requesting seamless skill syncing across surfaces).
evidence.author: meCodeUp

evidence.quote: Earlier this year, my co-founder and I found ourselves frequently switching between different coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) anytime we ran out of shaky usage limits or a newer model came out.
evidence.author: shakshukan

title: Multi-Account & Connector Profile Switcher for AI Coding CLIs
oneLiner: Switch cleanly between personal, freelance, and employer Claude Code / AI CLI accounts and connectors in one command.
problemSummary: Over 2,100 developers on GitHub upvoted feature requests to manage multiple accounts and multiple same-service connectors (e.g., personal vs. work GitHub/Slack/Claude accounts) without manually logging out and wiping credentials every time.
targetAudience: Consultants, contractors, and engineers separating personal and work AI CLI accounts

competitors.name: Claude Code
competitors.weakness: Lacks built-in multi-account profile switching and multi-tenant connector isolation per directory.

mvpScope: Isolated profile directories (`~/.ai-profiles/work`, `~/.ai-profiles/personal`) with safe env/config directory switching
Auto-switch active profile based on current Git directory (`.aiprofile` file, like `.nvmrc`)
Menu-bar status indicator (optional desktop wrapper) showing active account before sending prompts
monetizationModel: Open-source CLI free; $19 one-time macOS/Windows tray app with usage/quota tracker

buildSpec.prd: Create a zero-dependency Node/TypeScript CLI (`aiprofile`) that manages isolated config directories for AI coding CLIs, detects per-folder `.aiprofile` files on shell `cd`, and wraps commands with the selected profile's config path and connector set.
buildSpec.schema: local JSON config (~/.aiprofile/registry.json): profiles ([{ name, configDir, matchPaths, connectorPreset, labelColor }]).
buildSpec.prompt: Build a TypeScript CLI named `aiprofile` that lets developers switch isolated config profiles for AI coding CLIs per project directory. Support `init`, `add`, `use`, `status`, directory-based auto-detection (like direnv/nvm), and safe isolated environment variable execution.

evidence.quote: [FEATURE] Add the ability to manage multiple Claude accounts within the Claude Code CLI (1,456+ reactions from developers juggling work and personal accounts).
evidence.author: Agentic-Marketer

evidence.quote: [FEATURE] Support multiple Connector accounts (same connector, different accounts — 702+ reactions).
evidence.author: nathanmargaglio

oneLiner: A dead-simple replacement for the discontinued QuickBooks Self-Employed app—instant offline-tolerant invoice entry that never wipes your draft.
problemSummary: Solo contractors forced off QuickBooks Self-Employed into full QuickBooks Accounting complain about constant app freezes, confusing category clutter, and invoice forms that erase entered data when a validation error happens.
targetAudience: Self-employed contractors, tradespeople, solo freelancers who only need fast invoicing + simple expense categories

competitors.name: QuickBooks Accounting
competitors.weakness: Discontinued Self-Employed tier, slow/freezing mobile app, and unforgiving invoice entry that discards drafts on error.

mvpScope: Mobile-first PWA with instant local draft autosave (never loses line items if signal drops or a field has a typo)
1-tap repeat client & saved service line items + instant PDF/Stripe payment link sharing via SMS or email
Simple 1-click year-end CSV/PDF tax export for accountants (no double-entry accounting jargon)
monetizationModel: Free up to 3 invoices/month; $9/mo flat unlimited invoices & expense snapshotting

buildSpec.prd: Build a mobile-first Next.js PWA + Supabase invoicing app tailored for solo contractors. Persist every keystroke in IndexedDB before syncing to Supabase so drafts never disappear. Include client presets, instant PDF generation, Stripe Payment Link embedding, and simple expense categorization.

evidence.quote: Just switched from QuickBooks self employed app, which is no longer available. It is way less organized and way less intuitive than the self employed app. It is harder to find categories.

evidence.quote: Entries get erased if there’s an error without any chance to edit. The field rules are not obvious either. This non user friendly feature has wasted too much of my time.

evidence.quote: This app constantly freezes when you try to open it. Sometimes to the point it won't open at all and you have to go back to the office and enter data through the desktop version.

title: No-Login Browser PDF E-Signature Tool with Resizable Stylus Signing
oneLiner: Send and sign PDF contracts in any mobile or iPad browser with freely resizable signatures, EU date formats, and zero recipient app installs.
problemSummary: Users signing agreements on DocuSign complain about frozen signature fields, tiny auto-locked signatures that cannot be resized, broken iPad stylus signing from email links, and rigid US-only date formatting.
targetAudience: Freelancers, boutique agencies, landlords, and EU/UK small businesses sending simple contracts

competitors.name: DocuSign
competitors.weakness: Clunky mobile signing, auto-locked tiny signature boxes, iPad stylus issues from email links, and inflexible US date formatting.

mvpScope: Upload PDF, drag/resize signature, initials, and locale-aware date fields (DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY)
Send 1-click browser signing link—recipients draw smoothly with mouse, finger, or Apple Pencil with zero app download or account
Embed vector signature + SHA-256 audit certificate page into the final signed PDF
monetizationModel: Free 3 docs/month; $12/mo flat unlimited documents or $29 pack of 100 envelopes

buildSpec.prd: Build a clean browser e-signature app in Next.js + pdf-lib + HTML5 Canvas (Pointer Events for Apple Pencil/touch pressure). Senders place resizable fields and choose date locale; recipients open a signed token URL, draw/resize freely, and both parties receive the flattened PDF with an audit trail.
buildSpec.schema: tables: documents (id, owner_id, title, original_pdf_url, signed_pdf_url, date_format, status, sha256_hash), signers (id, document_id, email, token, signed_at, ip_address), fields (id, document_id, signer_id, type, page, x, y, width, height, value).
buildSpec.prompt: Build a Next.js + TypeScript PDF e-signature web app using pdf-lib and Pointer Events canvas. Support uploading a PDF, placing freely resizable signature and locale-formatted date fields (EU DD/MM/YYYY and US MM/DD/YYYY), zero-login recipient signing that works smoothly with Apple Pencil/iPad, and generating a tamper-evident signed PDF with an audit trail page.

evidence.quote: Signatures don’t save properly or fail to use your default signature... Also good luck trying to resize your signature. As the app seems to auto lock the signature size.

evidence.quote: Signing straight from email did not allow me to actually sign on an iPad with a stylus. Picked up some default signature for me. Could not use finger either.

evidence.quote: The error message about duplicate recipients isn’t helpful and doesn’t make sense. Someone needs to make a better alternative.

problemSummary: Service professionals using Calendly report blocked-off days still accepting bookings, sync errors after OS updates, and repeated login friction just to check who booked next.
targetAudience: Consultants, coaches, sales reps, and solo service providers managing multiple Google/Outlook calendars

competitors.name: Calendly
competitors.weakness: Users report appointments getting booked on blocked days, mobile view errors, and recurring login friction.

mvpScope: Real-time free/busy re-verification against all connected calendars right at booking submit time (atomic lock prevents double-booking)
One-tap 'Block Today / Block Week' emergency switch + persistent magic-link mobile agenda view
Simple booking page with buffer times, timezone auto-detection, and automatic Google Meet/Zoom link creation

buildSpec.prompt: Create a Next.js + TypeScript + Supabase appointment scheduler. Implement Google Calendar multi-calendar free/busy checks, strict blackout-date enforcement that re-validates availability atomically at submit time to prevent double bookings, buffer rules, and a clean mobile agenda view.

title: AI-Code Architecture Drift & Flow Audit Gate for Vibe Coders
oneLiner: Connect your GitHub repo to catch broken user flows, duplicated logic, and unreviewed AI spaghetti code before shipping to production.
problemSummary: Developers relying heavily on Claude Code and Cursor report losing mental visibility over architecture and user flows as AI writes most of the codebase, causing regressions and spiraling technical debt.
targetAudience: Indie hackers, solo founders, and engineering leads shipping AI-generated codebases

competitors.name: Generic AI PR Reviewers
competitors.weakness: Leave noisy line-by-line nitpicks instead of mapping end-to-end user flows, architecture boundaries, and missing edge-case tests.

mvpScope: GitHub App that scans every PR and generates a plain-English visual flow map + architecture diff
Flags silent auth/permission gaps, duplicated helpers, dead routes, and untested critical paths
Outputs a ready-to-paste remediation prompt for Claude Code / Cursor to fix the exact issues
monetizationModel: Free 1 public repo; $19/mo for unlimited private repos & PR checks

buildSpec.prd: Build a Next.js + GitHub App that hooks into pull_request events, builds a lightweight AST/route/schema graph of the repository, detects architectural drift and unprotected routes, and posts a concise PR comment with a Mermaid flow diagram and a copyable fix prompt.
buildSpec.schema: tables: repos (id, owner_id, github_repo_id, full_name, rules_md), audits (id, repo_id, pr_number, risk_score, findings_json, mermaid_graph, fix_prompt, created_at).
buildSpec.prompt: Build a Next.js + TypeScript GitHub App that audits AI-generated pull requests for architecture drift and broken user flows. Parse changed routes/APIs/schemas, identify auth gaps or duplicated logic, render a Mermaid flow diff, and output a targeted remediation prompt for Cursor/Claude Code.

evidence.quote: In the past when I wrote all the code manually, it was always carefully reviewed and architected, with all possible flows carefully mapped out. Now, my code is mostly AI written which has led to things going out of control.
evidence.author: nkcodes

title: Real-Time Rough Sketch to Clean Wireframe & SVG Canvas
oneLiner: Draw rough UI boxes on an iPad or trackpad and watch them snap into crisp, editable wireframes and React/Tailwind mockups in real time.
problemSummary: Designers and founders miss Tldraw's discontinued Draw Fast experiment and still struggle to find a fast canvas that converts messy hand-drawn sketches into clean, high-fidelity wireframes or vector illustrations in near real time.
targetAudience: Product designers, solo founders, and indie builders brainstorming UI wireframes on iPad or desktop

competitors.name: Tldraw Draw Fast
competitors.weakness: Experimental feature was shut down in 2024, leaving a direct gap for live sketch-to-wireframe workflows.

mvpScope: Split-screen iPad/touch-friendly drawing canvas (left) + live rendered wireframe preview (right)
Debounced stroke-to-image / stroke-to-SVG generation (< 1.5s latency via fast vision/diffusion endpoint)
One-click export to clean SVG, Figma-pasteable frames, or React + Tailwind starter component
monetizationModel: Free 15 generations/day; $15/mo unlimited live canvas + code export

buildSpec.prompt: Create a Next.js + TypeScript split-screen web app: a responsive Apple-Pencil-ready sketch canvas on the left and a live wireframe/UI preview on the right. Debounce canvas exports on stroke end, call a vision/code-gen API to render clean Tailwind HTML or SVG wireframes, and provide 1-click Copy SVG and Copy Tailwind Code buttons.

evidence.quote: I’ve been looking for a tool that can translate rough sketches on my iPad to higher fidelity wireframes or illustrations in near real time. The closest was Tldraw that shuttered their Draw Fast experiment in 2024.

problemSummary: Over 270 self-hosting readers upvoted Kobo sync support on Audiobookshelf because Kobo e-readers lack Kindle's send-to-email workflow and require clunky USB cables or manual Calibre-Web workarounds.
targetAudience: Self-hosted Audiobookshelf / Calibre users who own Kobo e-readers

Connects to Audiobookshelf API to convert EPUBs to KEPUB on the fly and push selected shelves to Kobo
Two-way reading progress sync back to the library server
